title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 8. The Passing of Jagannatha Mishra
html:
Murari's answer: the Lord enters the devotee's heart, and the devotee takes on His form (the examples of Prahlada, the gopis and Narada); Vishvambhara's studies; the illness and passing of Jagannatha Mishra on the bank of the Ganga; the funeral rites

Verse 1

इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य चिन्तयित्वा विचार्य च।
नत्वा हरिं पुनः प्राह शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः॥१॥

iti śrutvā vacastasya cintayitvā vicārya ca|
natvā hariṁ punaḥ prāha śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ||1||

iti — thus; shrutva — hearing; vachah — the words; tasya — his; chintayitva — having thought; vicharya — having reflected; cha — and; natva — bowing; harim — to Hari; punah — again; praha — said; shrinushva — listen; su-samahitah — with full attention.

1Having heard him, (Murari) thought and reflected, bowed to Hari and spoke again: "Listen with all your attention.

Verse 2

जनस्य भगवद्ध्यानात्कीर्तनाच्छ्रवणादपि।
हरेः प्रवेशो हृदये जायते सुमहात्मनः॥२॥

janasya bhagavaddhyānātkīrtanācchravaṇādapi|
hareḥ praveśo hṛdaye jāyate sumahātmanaḥ||2||

janasya — of a person; bhagavad-dhyanat — from meditation on Bhagavan; kirtanat — from kirtana; shravanat — from hearing; api — also; hareh — of Hari; praveshah — the entry; hridaye — into the heart; jayate — takes place; su-maha-atmanah — of a great soul.

2When a person meditates on Bhagavan, sings His kirtana and hears (of Him), Hari enters the heart of that great soul.

Verse 3

तस्यानुकारं चक्रे स तत्तेजस्तत्पराक्रमम्।
दधाति पुरुषो नित्यमात्मदेहादिविस्मृतः॥३॥

tasyānukāraṁ cakre sa tattejastatparākramam|
dadhāti puruṣo nityamātmadehādivismṛtaḥ||3||

tasya — of him; anukaram — imitation; chakre — makes; sah — he; tat-tejah — his splendour; tat-parakramam — his might; dadhati — bears; purushah — the person; nityam — constantly; atma-deha-adi-vismritah — forgetful of his own body and the rest.

3And then he imitates Him: forgetting his own body and all the rest, he constantly bears within him His splendour and His might.

Verse 4

भवेदेवं ततः काले पुनर्बाह्यो भवेत्ततः।
करोति सहजं कर्म प्रह्लादस्य यथा पुरा॥४॥

bhavedevaṁ tataḥ kāle punarbāhyo bhavettataḥ|
karoti sahajaṁ karma prahlādasya yathā purā||4||

bhavet — it happens; evam — so; tatah — then; kale — in time; punah — again; bahyah — in outer (consciousness); bhavet — becomes; tatah — then; karoti — does; sahajam — natural; karma — acts; prahladasya — with Prahlada; yatha — as; pura — once.

4So it is for a time; and then he returns to outer consciousness and does his ordinary acts — as once Prahlada did:

Verse 5

तादात्म्योऽभूत्तोयनिधौ पुनर्देहस्मृतिस्तटे।
एवं हि गोपसाध्वीनां तादात्म्यं सम्भवेत्क्वचित्॥५॥

tādātmyo'bhūttoyanidhau punardehasmṛtistaṭe|
evaṁ hi gopasādhvīnāṁ tādātmyaṁ sambhavetkvacit||5||

tadatmyah — identification (with the Lord); abhut — there was; toya-nidhau — in the ocean; punah — then; deha-smritih — remembrance of the body; tate — on the shore; evam — so; hi — indeed; gopa-sadhvinam — of the virtuous gopis; tadatmyam — identification; sambhavet — occurs; kvachit — at times.

5in the ocean he became identified (with the Lord), and on the shore the remembrance of his body returned1. So indeed the virtuous gopis too at times experience such identification2.

Verse 6

ईश्वरस्तस्य संशिक्षां दर्शयंस्तच्चकार ह।
लोकस्य कृष्णभक्तस्य भवेदेतत्स्वरूपता॥६॥

īśvarastasya saṁśikṣāṁ darśayaṁstaccakāra ha|
lokasya kṛṣṇabhaktasya bhavedetatsvarūpatā||6||

ishvarah — the Lord; tasya — of this; samshiksham — the teaching; darshayan — showing; tat — that; chakara ha — did; lokasya — to the world; krishna-bhaktasya — for a devotee of Krishna; bhavet — there can be; etat — this; svarupata — identity of form.

6The Lord did this to teach the world a lesson: for a devotee of Krishna there can be such identity of form (with Him).

Verse 7

यथात्र न विमुह्यन्ति जना इत्यभ्यशिक्षयत्।
भक्तदेहो भगवतो ह्यात्मा चैव न संशयः॥७॥

yathātra na vimuhyanti janā ityabhyaśikṣayat|
bhaktadeho bhagavato hyātmā caiva na saṁśayaḥ||7||

yatha — so that; atra — here; na vimuhyanti — are not bewildered; janah — people; iti — thus; abhyashikshayat — he taught; bhakta-dehah — the devotee's body; bhagavatah — of Bhagavan; hi — truly; atma — the self; cha eva — and; na samshayah — there is no doubt.

7And so that people here should not be bewildered, He taught: the devotee's body is truly the very self of Bhagavan3; of this there is no doubt.

Verse 8

कृष्णः केशिवधं कृत्वा नारदायात्मनो यशः।
तेजश्च दर्शयामास ततो मुनिवरो भुवि॥८॥

kṛṣṇaḥ keśivadhaṁ kṛtvā nāradāyātmano yaśaḥ|
tejaśca darśayāmāsa tato munivaro bhuvi||8||

krishnah — Krishna; keshi-vadham — the slaying of Keshi; kritva — having accomplished; naradaya — to Narada; atmanah — his own; yashah — glory; tejah — power; cha — and; darshayamasa — showed; tatah — then; muni-varah — the best of sages; bhuvi — to the ground.

8Krishna, having slain Keshi, showed Narada His glory and His power; and then the best of sages

Verse 9

पपात दण्डवत्तस्मिन्स्थाने शतगुणाधिकम्।
फलमाप्नोति गत्वा तु वैष्णवो मथुरां पुरीम्॥९॥

papāta daṇḍavattasminsthāne śataguṇādhikam|
phalamāpnoti gatvā tu vaiṣṇavo mathurāṁ purīm||9||

papata — fell; danda-vat — like a stick; tasmin — in that; sthane — place; shata-guna-adhikam — a hundredfold greater; phalam — reward; apnoti — obtains; gatva — going; tu — and; vaishnavah — a Vaishnava; mathuram — to Mathura; purim — the city.

9fell to the ground like a stick. And a Vaishnava who goes to the city of Mathura obtains at that place a hundredfold greater reward4.

Verse 10

एवं रामो जगद्योनिर्विश्वरूपमदर्शयत्।
शिवाय पुनरेवासौ मानुषीमकरोत्क्रियाम्॥१०॥

evaṁ rāmo jagadyonirviśvarūpamadarśayat|
śivāya punarevāsau mānuṣīmakarotkriyām||10||

evam — so; ramah — Rama; jagad-yonih — the source of the world; vishvarupam — the universal form; adarshayat — showed; shivaya — to Shiva; punah — then again; eva — indeed; asau — he; manushim — human; akarot — performed; kriyam — action.

10So too Rama, the source of the world, showed His universal form to Shiva, and then again performed human deeds5.

Verse 11

पुनः शृणुष्व भो ब्रह्मंश्चैतन्यस्य कथां शुभाम्।
यच्छ्रुत्वा श्रद्धया मर्त्यो मुच्यते भवबन्धनात्॥११॥

punaḥ śṛṇuṣva bho brahmaṁścaitanyasya kathāṁ śubhām|
yacchrutvā śraddhayā martyo mucyate bhavabandhanāt||11||

punah — further; shrinushva — hear; bhoh brahman — O brahmana; chaitanyasya — of Chaitanya; katham — the story; shubham — auspicious; yat — which; shrutva — hearing; shraddhaya — with faith; martyah — a mortal; muchyate — is freed; bhava-bandhanat — from the bondage of worldly existence.

11Now, O brahmana, hear further the auspicious story of Chaitanya: whoever hears it with faith, though mortal, is freed from the bondage of worldly existence.

Verse 12

गुरोर्गृहे वसञ्जिष्णुर्वेदान्सर्वानधीतवान्।
पाठयामास शिष्यान्स सरस्वतीपतिः स्वयम्॥१२॥

gurorgṛhe vasañjiṣṇurvedānsarvānadhītavān|
pāṭhayāmāsa śiṣyānsa sarasvatīpatiḥ svayam||12||

guroh — of the teacher; grihe — in the house; vasan — living; jishnuh — the Victorious; vedan — the Vedas; sarvan — all; adhitavan — studied; pathayamasa — taught; shishyan — students; sah — he; sarasvati-patih — the husband of Sarasvati (lord of learning); svayam — himself.

12Living in the house of His teacher, the Victorious One studied all the Vedas, and then He Himself, the husband of Sarasvati6, taught students.

Verse 13

तत्पितापि महाभागो वेदान्तादीन्पठन्सुखी।
ततश्च पुनरायातो जगन्नाथो द्विजर्षभः॥१३॥

tatpitāpi mahābhāgo vedāntādīnpaṭhansukhī|
tataśca punarāyāto jagannātho dvijarṣabhaḥ||13||

tat-pita — his father; api — and; maha-bhagah — greatly fortunate; vedanta-adin — Vedanta and the rest; pathan — studying; sukhi — happy; tatah cha — and then; punah — again; ayatah — returned (home); jagannathah — Jagannatha; dvija-rshabhah — the bull among brahmanas.

13His father too, greatly fortunate, happily studied the Vedanta and other scriptures. And when Jagannatha, the bull among brahmanas, had returned (home),

Verse 14

दैवयोगेन तस्याभूज्ज्वरः प्राणापहारकः।
अतस्तं तादृशं दृष्ट्वा सह मात्रा स्वयं हरिः॥१४॥

daivayogena tasyābhūjjvaraḥ prāṇāpahārakaḥ|
atastaṁ tādṛśaṁ dṛṣṭvā saha mātrā svayaṁ hariḥ||14||

daiva-yogena — by the will of fate; tasya — to him; abhut — there came; jvarah — a fever; prana-apaharakah — life-taking; atah — therefore; tam — him; tadrisham — in such a state; drishtva — seeing; saha — together; matra — with the mother; svayam — himself; harih — Hari.

14by the will of fate a life-taking fever came upon him. Seeing His father in such a state, Hari Himself, together with His mother,

Verse 15

जगाम जाह्नवीतीरे निजभक्तैः समावृतः।
श्रीमान्विश्वम्भरो देवो हरिकीर्तनतत्परैः॥१५॥

jagāma jāhnavītīre nijabhaktaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ|
śrīmānviśvambharo devo harikīrtanatatparaiḥ||15||

jagama — went; jahnavi-tire — to the bank of the Jahnavi; nija-bhaktaih — by his devotees; samavritah — surrounded; shriman — the beautiful; vishvambharah — Vishvambhara; devah — the Lord; hari-kirtana-tatparaih — absorbed in the kirtana of Hari.

15went to the bank of the Jahnavi — the beautiful Lord Vishvambhara, surrounded by His devotees absorbed in the kirtana of Hari.

Verse 16

अथ तस्य पदद्वयं हरिः पितुरालिङ्ग्य सगद्गदस्वरम्।
अवदत्पितराशु मां प्रभो परिहाय क्व भवान्गमिष्यसि॥१६॥

atha tasya padadvayaṁ hariḥ piturāliṅgya sagadgadasvaram|
avadatpitarāśu māṁ prabho parihāya kva bhavāngamiṣyasi||16||

atha — then; tasya — his; pada-dvayam — two feet; harih — Hari; pituh — of the father; alingya — embracing; sa-gadgada-svaram — in a faltering voice; avadat — said; pitah — father; ashu — so soon; mam — me; prabho — O master; parihaya — leaving; kva — where; bhavan — you; gamishyasi — will go.

16Then Hari embraced both His father's feet and said in a faltering voice: 'Father, My master! Where are you going, leaving Me so soon?'

Verse 17

इति वागमृतं सुतस्य स श्रवणाभ्यां परिपीय सादरम्।
अवदद्रघुनाथपादयोस्तव सम्यक्सुसमर्पणं कृतम्॥१७॥

iti vāgamṛtaṁ sutasya sa śravaṇābhyāṁ paripīya sādaram|
avadadraghunāthapādayostava samyaksusamarpaṇaṁ kṛtam||17||

iti — thus; vak-amritam — the nectar of the words; sutasya — of the son; sah — he; shravanabhyam — with his ears; paripiya — drinking; sa-adaram — lovingly; avadat — said; raghunatha-padayoh — to the feet of Raghunatha; tava — of you; samyak — fully; su-samarpanam — entrusting; kritam — is done.

17He lovingly drank in with his ears the nectar of his son's words and replied: 'I have entrusted You wholly to the feet of Raghunatha.'7

Verse 18

गगने सुरवर्यसंहतौ समहेन्द्रे समुपस्थिते दिवा।
हरिसंकीर्तनतत्परे जने द्युनदीतोयगतो द्विजोत्तमः॥१८॥

gagane suravaryasaṁhatau samahendre samupasthite divā|
harisaṁkīrtanatatpare jane dyunadītoyagato dvijottamaḥ||18||

gagane — in the sky; sura-varya-samhatau — when the host of the best gods; sa-mahendre — with Mahendra; samupasthite — had appeared; diva — by day; hari-sankirtana-tatpare — absorbed in the sankirtana of Hari; jane — when the people (were); dyu-nadi-toya-gatah — being in the waters of the heavenly river; dvija-uttamah — the best of brahmanas.

18By day, when the host of the best gods with Mahendra had appeared in the sky and the people were absorbed in the sankirtana of Hari, the best of brahmanas, standing in the waters of the heavenly river,

Verse 19

परिहाय तनुं दिवौकसां रथमास्थाय ययौ हरेः पुरीम्।
नित्यसिद्धशरीरोऽपि महात्मा लोकहिताचरणाय यथासुखम्॥१९॥

parihāya tanuṁ divaukasāṁ rathamāsthāya yayau hareḥ purīm|
nityasiddhaśarīro'pi mahātmā lokahitācaraṇāya yathāsukham||19||

parihaya — leaving; tanum — the body; divau-kasam — of the heaven-dwellers; ratham — the chariot; asthaya — mounting; yayau — went; hareh — of Hari; purim — to the abode; nitya-siddha-sharirah — possessing an eternally perfect body; api — though; maha-atma — the great soul; loka-hita-acharanaya — for conduct beneficial to the world; yatha-sukham — at his will.

19left his body, mounted the chariot of the heaven-dwellers and went to the abode of Hari. Though the body of that great soul is eternally perfect, he (showed death) at his own will, so that his conduct might serve the good of the world.

Verse 20

अथ सिद्धिगतं पतिं शची परिदीना विललाप दुःखिता।
चरणे विनिपत्य सा प्रभोः कुररीव प्रमदागणावृता॥२०॥

atha siddhigataṁ patiṁ śacī paridīnā vilalāpa duḥkhitā|
caraṇe vinipatya sā prabhoḥ kurarīva pramadāgaṇāvṛtā||20||

atha — then; siddhi-gatam — who had attained perfection; patim — for her husband; shachi — Shachi; paridina — utterly wretched; vilalapa — lamented; duhkhita — grieving; charane — at the feet; vinipatya — falling; sa — she; prabhoh — of her lord (husband); kurari — an osprey; iva — like; pramada-gana-avrita — surrounded by a crowd of women.

20Then Shachi, utterly broken by grief, lamented her husband who had attained perfection; surrounded by a crowd of women, she fell at the feet of her lord and cried out like an osprey.

Verse 21

पितरं विलपतो मुहुर्दृशोरपतद्वारिझरो दयानिधेः।
गजमौक्तिकहारविभ्रमं विदधद्वक्षसि लक्षणं बभौ॥२१॥

pitaraṁ vilapato muhurdṛśorapatadvārijharo dayānidheḥ|
gajamauktikahāravibhramaṁ vidadhadvakṣasi lakṣaṇaṁ babhau||21||

pitaram — for his father; vilapatah — of him who lamented; muhuh — again and again; drishoh — from the eyes; apatat — fell; vari-jharah — a stream of tears; daya-nidheh — of the treasury of mercy; gaja-mauktika-hara-vibhramam — resembling a necklace of elephant-pearls; vidadhat — making; vakshasi — on the chest; lakshanam — a mark; babhau — shone.

21As the ocean of mercy wept again and again for His father, streams of tears fell from His eyes; leaving on His chest a trace like a necklace of elephant-pearls8, they shone.

Verse 22

अथ बन्धुजनैः प्रशान्तितः परिणामोचितसत्क्रियां प्रभुः।
अकरोत्परिवेदनान्वितो विधिदृष्ट्या सकलां सह द्विजैः॥२२॥

atha bandhujanaiḥ praśāntitaḥ pariṇāmocitasatkriyāṁ prabhuḥ|
akarotparivedanānvito vidhidṛṣṭyā sakalāṁ saha dvijaiḥ||22||

atha — then; bandhu-janaih — by his relatives; prashantitah — consoled; parinama-uchita-sat-kriyam — the holy rites fitting for the end of life; prabhuh — the Lord; akarot — performed; parivedana-anvitah — full of grief; vidhi-drishtya — according to the injunctions; sakalam — all; saha — together; dvijaih — with brahmanas.

22Then, consoled by His relatives, the Lord, full of grief, performed together with the brahmanas all the holy rites fitting for the end of life, according to the injunctions.

Verse 23

विमना इव सञ्चितैर्धनैः पितृयज्ञं पितृवत्सलोऽकरोत्।
द्विजपूजनसत्क्रियां क्रमाद्विदधे तां स धरादिभाजनैः॥२३॥

vimanā iva sañcitairdhanaiḥ pitṛyajñaṁ pitṛvatsalo'karot|
dvijapūjanasatkriyāṁ kramādvidadhe tāṁ sa dharādibhājanaiḥ||23||

vimanah — downcast; iva — as if; sanchitaih — with the accumulated; dhanaih — wealth; pitri-yajnam — the sacrifice to the ancestors (shraddha); pitri-vatsalah — loving his father; akarot — performed; dvija-pujana-sat-kriyam — the holy rite of honouring brahmanas; kramat — in due order; vidadhe — performed; tam — that; sah — he; dhara-adi-bhajanaih — with gifts of land and other things (?).

23As if downcast, loving His father, He performed with the accumulated wealth the sacrifice to the ancestors, and then in due order the holy rite of honouring the brahmanas, presenting them with land and other gifts9.

Verse 24

इति यो वदति प्रभोः पितुर्दिवसंस्थानमतन्द्रितो नरः।
लभते द्युनदीं हरेः पुरीं परिहायाशु मलं स गच्छति॥२४॥

iti yo vadati prabhoḥ piturdivasaṁsthānamatandrito naraḥ|
labhate dyunadīṁ hareḥ purīṁ parihāyāśu malaṁ sa gacchati||24||

iti — thus; yah — who; vadati — tells; prabhoh — of the Lord; pituh — of the father; diva-samsthanam — the departure to heaven; atandritah — tirelessly; narah — a person; labhate — obtains; dyu-nadim — the heavenly river (Ganga); hareh — of Hari; purim — to the abode; parihaya — casting off; ashu — swiftly; malam — impurity; sah — he; gachchhati — goes.

24Whoever tirelessly tells thus of the departure to heaven of the Lord's father will attain the heavenly river and, swiftly casting off impurity, will go to the abode of Hari."

Thus ends the eighth sarga, "The Passing of Jagannatha Mishra" (Jagannatha-mishra-samsiddhi), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Prahlada, thrown into the ocean at Hiranyakashipu's command, became so absorbed in meditation on the Lord that he forgot himself and felt himself to be Him; on the shore he again became aware of his body.
  2. The gopis, in separation from Krishna, imitated His pastimes, identifying themselves with Him (Bhagavata Purana 10.30). Such "identification" (tadatmya) is love's complete absorption in the Lord, not the dissolution of the devotee in God: it lasts only for a time, and the devotee again serves the Lord (v. 4).
  3. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 9.4.68: "The saints are My heart, and I am their heart." The devotee is so dear to the Lord and so filled with Him that the Lord regards him as His own self; this does not mean that the devotee becomes God.
  4. The place where the demon Keshi was slain in Vrindavana is revered as holy (Keshi-ghat in Vrindavana, in the land of Mathura).
  5. Rama is Ramachandra, the avatara of Vishnu; Shiva is His great worshipper.
  6. The husband of Sarasvati (the goddess of learning) — the Lord as master of all knowledge.
  7. Raghunatha ("Lord of the Raghus") is Ramachandra.
  8. By poetic convention, pearls are born in the foreheads of elephants.
  9. The sense of the word "dharadibhajanaih" is unclear; the translation is tentative.
